name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu

phases.title: The French fortress and the Viet Minh ring
phases.text: The French held a central headquarters with strong points round it, and Isabelle to the south. The Viet Minh moved divisions and artillery into the hills round the valley and the French were completely surrounded.

phases.title: Béatrice is overrun
phases.text: The Viet Minh opened with a heavy bombardment of Béatrice, the northeastern outpost. The 312th Division then attacked, and by the early hours of 14 March the position had been taken.

phases.title: Gabrielle falls and Anne-Marie is given up
phases.text: The 308th Division attacked Gabrielle on the night of 14 March, and the Algerian battalion fell back at 08:00 the next day. On 17 March most of the Tai troops left or defected, and Anne-Marie was abandoned.

phases.title: Attacks on the eastern and western positions
phases.text: The 312th Division took Dominique 1 and 2 and the 316th Division took Eliane 1. In the west the 308th Division nearly broke through at Huguette 7, but the breach was sealed.

phases.title: Trenches and sapping
phases.text: After heavy losses in open ground on 5 April, Giáp turned to entrenchment and sapping. The Viet Minh trenches almost surrounded Huguette 1 and 6, and Huguette 1 was overrun on 22 April.

phases.title: The eastern positions are overrun
phases.text: On the night of 1 May the Viet Minh overran Eliane 1 and Dominique 3, and on 6 May they attacked Eliane 2 with Katyusha rockets. A mine under Eliane 2 was detonated and within a few hours the defenders were overrun.

phases.title: The last attack on the headquarters
phases.text: Giáp ordered an all-out attack on the remaining French units. By evening enemy troops stood outside the headquarters bunker and the last radio report said the positions had been overrun.

note: The plan shows the whole siege, not a single day: the blocks are the strong points and the Viet Minh divisions. The positions of the strong points follow the compass directions the accounts give; the distances are not to scale except that Isabelle stands furthest south. The accounts do not say where each Viet Minh division stood before it attacked, so each is placed in the hills on the side of the strong point it is said to have attacked. Claudine, Eliane and the other numbered works are not drawn singly. Isabelle's end is told only as a breakout, so its block is left as it was.
